scope: Independent exact-content technical review of the Fortinet hardening article, master PNG and primary sources. This is not publication, deployment, customer-appliance validation or a CCNA review.

masterImage.pixelInspection: Performed by this reviewer using the actual PNG.

manifest.scope: Source inventory and target mapping; pending publication/workflow fields were not independently tested as external system state.

checks.verification: Read the complete JSON, including definitions, all ten sections, all five FAQs, checklist, source mappings, metadata and visual brief.
The announcement, affected ranges, product distinctions and pending-disclosure boundaries match the live primary evidence.
All four FortiOS versions/builds were checked directly; general builds are distinguished from model-specific images.
All three literal commands match Fortinet's reference and are appropriately described as observational checks.
The 7.6.8-specific behavior is accurately scoped; larger-transfer testing is explicitly a recommendation, not observed runtime.
Recovery access, protected backups, model-specific paths, HA/Fabric boundaries, known issues and escalation are explicit; no generic destructive upgrade/downgrade command is supplied.
All eleven article/manifest bibliography URLs were opened live and their relevant content read; section/FAQ mappings refer to listed sources.

Inspected the actual 2400x1350 master PNG. Four independent branch tracks, ranges, targets, disclosure date and supported-path caveats match the article. Text is readable with no observed overlap or clipping.
Schema passes. Hypothetical and unexecuted tests are labelled honestly. The pending-review metadata is accurate for the submitted draft and may now be finalized truthfully.

verifiedSources.label: Fortinet: October 21 security-hardening announcement
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live October 21 announcement. Confirmed the October 22 coordinated release, critical/high characterization, all four affected FortiOS ranges and targets, distinct FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer target rows, temporary exposure controls, and planned November 10 advisories. It does not establish individual CVEs, scores, prerequisites or active exploitation.

verifiedSources.label: FortiOS 7.2.14: introduction and supported models
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live release introduction in the browser. Confirmed 7.2.14 general build 1778, supported models and separate special-branch builds; the article correctly requires model-specific checking.

verifiedSources.label: FortiOS 7.4.13: introduction and supported models
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live release introduction in the browser. Confirmed 7.4.13 general build 2933 and model-specific special builds; the hypothetical 7.4.12 example is within the announced affected range.

verifiedSources.label: FortiOS 7.6.8: introduction and supported models
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live release introduction in the browser. Confirmed 7.6.8 general build 3744, supported models and cloud-instance caveats; no universal appliance compatibility is claimed.

verifiedSources.label: FortiOS 8.0.2: introduction and supported models
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live release introduction in the browser. Confirmed 8.0.2 general build 0251 and supported-model restrictions. The article does not tell every device to move to this branch.

verifiedSources.label: FortiOS 7.6.8: supported upgrade-path guidance
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live upgrade guidance in the browser. Confirmed the Upgrade Path Tool takes product, model, current version and target; individual-device and Security Fabric procedures are distinguished.

verifiedSources.label: FortiOS 7.6.8: changes in default behavior
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live default-behavior note in the browser. Bug 1073893 documents the large-TCP/IPsec MSS behavior and ICMP_FRAG_NEEDED feedback. The article confines the claim to 7.6.8 and labels its transfer test as an inference, not a reproduced failure.

verifiedSources.label: FortiOS 7.6.8: known issues
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live known-issues page in the browser, including HA, IPsec, platform, system and VM entries. It supports checking deployment-specific limitations and does not establish that every upgrade fails.

verifiedSources.label: Fortinet: CLI troubleshooting cheat sheet
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live CLI cheat sheet in the browser. Confirmed get system status for system information, get system performance status for CPU/memory and get system ha status for HA information. These are the article's three literal CLI commands; none was executed.

verifiedSources.label: Fortinet: troubleshooting methodology
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live troubleshooting-methodology page in the browser. Confirmed permission checks, recording a normal baseline, the stated system-information commands, problem scoping, checklist/evidence collection and support escalation.

verifiedSources.label: FortiGuard PSIRT advisory index
verifiedSources.verification: Read the live PSIRT index in the browser. The visible relevant October 13 records include FG-IR-26-178 SQL injection affecting FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer. This is distinct from the coordinated hardening notice; the index is not evidence of exploit status for the undisclosed fixes.
Followed the release guidance to the individual-device procedure. Confirmed backup, intermediate-path advice, direct-upgrade configuration-loss warning and firmware signature validation.
Followed the documented download link. Confirmed authorized support-site acquisition, matching the model and release notes, HTTPS preference and integrity-checking references.

Followed the documented downgrade link. Confirmed downgrade is discouraged, HA interruption is possible and restoration compatibility is not guaranteed; the article appropriately defers to platform-specific recovery procedures.

Read the primary-source search excerpt describing vendor firmware checksums available through the support portal. Used only to corroborate the general checksum recommendation; no firmware binary or portal checksum was obtained or tested.

metadataFinalization.conditions: The author may record this actual independent source-based review, retain the no-runtime statement and use actual publication/update dates. Do not imply human, Fortinet, appliance-runtime or website-deployment approval. This receipt's raw SHA remains the reviewed input, not the hash of a subsequently edited file.
metadataFinalization.digestMethod: Parse article JSON, remove only top-level reviewedBy, editorialMethod, publishedAt and updatedAt, recursively sort object keys lexicographically, preserve array order, JSON.stringify without whitespace, then SHA256 of UTF-8.
metadataFinalization.releaseHandoff: Any metadata-finalized article must retain this substantive digest and the exact master-image hash; record its final raw hash separately. Any other change requires renewed content review.

limitations: No FortiGate appliance, emulator, GNS3, CML, HA failover, firmware installation, command execution, exploit test or application-network runtime was performed.
Source browsing and master-PNG pixel inspection were performed; live QCS page rendering, accessibility, publication HTTP checks and social-platform QA were not performed by this review.

The web retrieval tool returned access errors for Fortinet documentation and PSIRT pages; their contents were successfully verified through the live browser instead. The supplemental checksum reference was checked through a primary-domain search excerpt only.
No authenticated firmware download, model-specific customer upgrade-path computation, license entitlement or vendor checksum comparison was performed.
Security applicability remains bounded by the current vendor announcement. Detailed advisories are pending; no claim of active exploitation or absence of prior compromise is established.
No author content, manifest, captions, posts, schedules, CCNA files, production files or database records were changed. No paid API was called.
Only the two independent-review receipt files were written. Publication and metadata finalization remain with the author/parent.
